transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because… it’s this airplane thing. I mean, I know people fly every day, and I used to think about all the statistics and how you hear that driving is more dangerous—though I don’t even know who calculates those things—but now just the thought of getting on a plane scares me so badly.

It doesn’t make sense to me, I can say that. But my body just reacts like that plane is going to fall out of the sky.
Is it just airplanes that scare you, or are there other situations that provoke a similar fear?

It’s really the airplanes. I mean, I can get nervous about plenty of things like anyone, but this is the one that… I don’t know, it just grabs me. Even thinking about getting on a plane, my body reacts like it’s certain the plane is going to fall, even though the rational part of me knows that doesn’t make sense.

I’ve tried telling myself all the usual things, and I hear people say flying is safe, but it doesn’t seem to matter. It’s the airplane thing that brings me here.
Has this fear of airplanes been affecting your daily life or causing you significant distress?

Yes. I mean, I wish I could say it’s just an inconvenience, but it’s been costing me. I’ve turned down coverage opportunities when they’d involve flying, and that’s meant less income. And then people start wondering if I’m dependable, you know—colleagues asking around or making little comments.

And it’s not just work. I’ve missed professional meetings I really should’ve gone to, the kind where everyone else seems to show up and talk afterward like it was nothing. And I’ve put off seeing family because getting there would mean a flight. So… yeah, it’s affecting things more than I’d like to admit.
Have you noticed this kind of intense fear reaction in situations other than flying?

Not really, no. I mean, I can get worked up about other things like anybody, but this particular kind of fear… it’s the airplane.

Just the thought of getting on one now scares me so badly. And I know, sitting here, that it doesn’t really make sense—I’ve even gone over that in my head—but my body reacts like the plane is definitely going to fall. It’s strange, because I can say the logical part out loud, but it doesn’t change what happens inside.
How long have you been experiencing this intense fear of airplanes?

About seven months now, I think. It started after this really bad turbulent flight on a small plane… right after I’d lost my clinic job, which was its own whole mess. I keep thinking maybe if that hadn’t happened at that time, I wouldn’t have reacted the same way, but—yeah, roughly seven months.
Do you worry about other modes of transportation, like cars, trains, or boats, in a similar way?

No, not like that. I mean, I don’t love traffic or anything, and boats can be unpleasant if it’s rough, but it doesn’t hit me the same way.

It’s really the airplane. I came in because just the thought of getting on one now scares me so badly that—honestly—I know it doesn’t make sense, but my body acts like the plane is going to fall. Like it’s already decided that’s what’s going to happen.
Does your fear of airplanes ever decrease or go away when you're not thinking about flying or an upcoming flight?

If I’m not thinking about it, I guess it can fade into the background, yeah. But it comes back immediately if something reminds me.

Like even just getting an email about a rural shift that would need a flight—before I’ve even really read the whole thing—my heart starts pounding, my hands get sweaty, and I feel like I can’t breathe until I close the message. It’s ridiculous because it’s just an email, not even the airport, but my body reacts like it’s happening right then.
Have you ever had a sudden episode where you felt an intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes, with symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or feeling like you can't breathe?

Yes—well, I don’t know if I’d call it an “episode” exactly, but it happens fast. Like if I get an email about some rural shift and I realize it would involve a flight, before I’ve even thought it through my heart is pounding, my hands are sweating, and I feel like I can’t breathe.

I usually end up closing the message just to make it stop. Then I feel kind of foolish, because it’s only an email, not like I’m actually on the plane.
Is your fear response triggered by the actual presence of an airplane, or can it be triggered just by thinking about airplanes or seeing pictures of them?

It can definitely happen just from thinking about it, not only when I’m near an actual airplane. Like, even an email about a rural shift where I’d have to fly—before I’ve really even processed it—my heart starts pounding right away, my hands get sweaty, and I feel like I can’t breathe until I close it.

Which is embarrassing, honestly, because it’s just an email. I get emails all day for work, schedules and coverage and all that, but if there’s anything about needing a flight, my body just reacts.
Have you ever had an intense, irrational fear of anything else, like spiders, heights, or enclosed spaces?

I don’t think so… not in the same way. I mean, I don’t love heights, but who does, right? And spiders are unpleasant, I guess, especially if one shows up in the bathroom at 2 a.m., but I wouldn’t say it takes over.

It’s more—sorry, I’m getting off track—it’s really the flying thing that stands out. Other stuff I can usually just deal with or ignore.
Does your fear of airplanes also extend to situations or places related to flying, such as airports?

Yes, the airport is… honestly, that’s almost as bad as the plane part. I’ve canceled clinic coverage before when it meant I’d have to fly, and I’ve skipped medical meetings too, even ones I probably should’ve gone to.

And my family is in Honduras, and I keep putting off visiting them because I just can’t make myself go to the airport. I mean, unless someone is right there with me and I’m basically shaking and holding on to them the whole time, I can’t do it. It sounds ridiculous when I say it out loud, but that’s what happens.
Does your fear start as soon as you know you have to travel, or is it specifically when you think about the flight itself?

It starts as soon as I know, really. Like if I just get an email saying there’s a rural shift and it would involve a flight, I don’t even have to be looking at tickets yet or anything. My heart starts pounding right away, my hands get sweaty, and I feel like I can’t breathe until I close the message.

And then I’ll try to tell myself, “Just answer the email,” because, I mean, it’s just work scheduling, I deal with messages all day… but if it means flying, my body reacts before I can talk myself out of it.
Have you ever had any other intense, irrational fears besides the one related to airplanes?

I don’t think there’s anything else like that, no. I mean, I can get uneasy about normal things—like, I don’t enjoy being stuck in traffic, and hospitals have their own stress, obviously, but that’s work-related and everybody’s tense there sometimes.

But in terms of some other big fear that makes me avoid things or panic the way airplanes do… I’m not coming up with one. It really seems tied to flying.
